A [[center (basketball)|center]], Gadzuric attended preparatory school at [[The Governor's Academy]] in [[Byfield, Massachusetts]], before playing [[college basketball]] for the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|Bruins]] at [[University of California, Los Angeles]] (UCLA). He was drafted by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in the [[2002 NBA draft]]. == Professional career == [[File:Dan Gadzuric.jpg|thumb|Gadzuric with the Milwaukee Bucks in 2006]] Gadzuric was drafted as the 34th overall pick by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] during the [[2002 NBA draft]]. On June 22, 2010, Gadzuric and [[Charlie Bell (basketball)|Charlie Bell]] were traded to the [[Golden State Warriors]] for [[Corey Maggette]]{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors_acquire_bell_gadzuric_062210.html |title=Warriors Acquire Charlie Bell And Dan Gadzuric From Milwaukee |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=June 22, 2010 |access-date=June 23, 2010}} after spending eight years with the Bucks. On February 23, 2011, Gadzuric was traded to the [[New Jersey Nets]] along with [[Brandan Wright]] in exchange for [[Troy Murphy]] and a second round pick.{{Cite web| title = NETS Acquire F Wright and C Gadzuric from Golden State | url = http://www.nba.com/nets/news/Warriors_Trade_Release_110223.html | date = February 23, 2011 | access-date = February 24, 2011 | work =[[NBA.com]]}} In October 2011, he signed with the [[Jiangsu Dragons]] in China.[http://www.sportando.net/eng/world/asia/31472/dan_gadzuric_inks_with_jiangsu.html Dan Gadzuric inks with Jiangsu] He was signed by the [[New York Knicks]] on April 20, 2012.{{Cite web| title=Amare back, Gadzuric added | url=https://www.espn.com/blog/new-york/knicks/post/_/id/17187/amare-back-gadzuric-added | date=April 20, 2012 | access-date=April 20, 2012 | work=[[ESPN.com]]}} This ended up being his final season in the NBA, as Gadzuric's final game was on April 26, 2012, in a 104–84 win over the Charlotte Bobcats where he recorded 3 rebounds, 1 steal and 1 block. On July 16, 2012, Gadzuric, [[Jared Jeffries]], the rights to [[Giorgos Printezis]] and [[Kostas Papanikolaou]] and a [[2016 NBA Draft|2016]] second round pick were traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] for [[Kurt Thomas (basketball)|Kurt Thomas]] and [[Raymond Felton]].{{cite web|url=http://www.iamatrailblazersfan.com/PressReleaseDisplay/tabid/297/itemId/3179/Default.aspx|title=Trail Blazers Acquire Jared Jeffries From New York|work=iamatrailblazersfan.com|date=July 16, 2012|access-date=July 16, 2012|url-status=usurped|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120719054058/http://www.iamatrailblazersfan.com/PressReleaseDisplay/tabid/297/itemId/3179/Default.aspx|archive-date=July 19, 2012}} On July 19, 2012, Gadzuric was waived by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].[http://www.blazersedge.com/2012/7/19/3170091/blazers-officially-waive-c-dan-gadzuric Blazers Officially Waive C Dan Gadzuric] In September 2012, he joined the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] for their training camp.[http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/sixers-announce-2012-training-camp-roster Sixers Announce 2012 Training Camp Roster] However, he did not make their final roster.{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=11198 |title=Sixers waive center Dan Gadzuric |access-date=October 19, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121020042315/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=11198 |archive-date=October 20, 2012 |url-status=dead }} In February 2013, he joined the [[Marinos de Anzoátegui]] of the Venezuelan [[Liga Profesional de Baloncesto]] (LPB).{{Cite web |url=http://www.court-side.com/news/blog/dan-gadzuric-signs-with-anzoategui/ |title=Dan Gadzuric signs with Anzoátegui |access-date=March 1, 2013 |archive-date=April 24, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130424111830/http://www.court-side.com/news/blog/dan-gadzuric-signs-with-anzoategui/ |url-status=dead }} With Marinos, he went on to lose the LPB finals to [[Cocodrilos de Caracas]] after a seven-game series. On September 27, 2013, he signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14353 |title=Lakers add Dan Gadzuric to training camp |access-date=September 28, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131101094946/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14353 |archive-date=November 1, 2013 |url-status=dead }} However, he was waived on October 9.[http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/100909_boateng_gadzuric Lakers Waive Eric Boateng and Dan Gadzuric] == National team career == Gadzuric played for the {{bklink|Netherlands}}. He made his debut on December 26, 1997, in an exhibition game against {{bklink|Cuba}} at the Haarlem Basketball Week.{{cite web|url=https://www.nfleurope.nl/basketball/internationaal/dan-gadzuric-speelt-eerste-oranje-interland-sinds-1997|title=Gadzuric speelt eerste Oranje interland sinds 1997 – NFLEurope.nl|date=August 2011 |access-date=September 20, 2019}} He went scoreless in 10 minutes of play, and it took ten years until he played another game with the Netherlands. In 2011, he played in another friendly game at the EuroJam 2011 tournament.{{cite web|url=https://www.nu.nl/sport-overig/2589627/rentree-gadzuric-hoogtepunt-eurojam-2011.html|title=Rentree Gadzuric hoogtepunt EuroJam 2011 – NU – Het laatste nieuws het eerst op NU.nl|date=August 15, 2011|work=www.nu.nl|access-date=September 20, 2019}} Gadzuric only played a few [[FIBA]] official games for his national team. == Family == Gadzuric's mother is from [[Belgrade]], [[Serbia]]{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/features/gaduric_chat_090220.html |author=[[Milwaukee Bucks]] |title=Chat with Dan Gadzuric |website=[[NBA.com]] |accessdate=February 12, 2021 |date=February 20, 2009 |language=English |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090310080449/http://www.nba.com/bucks/features/gaduric_chat_090220.html |archive-date=March 10, 2009 |url-status=dead }} and his father is from [[Kingstown]], [[St. Vincent and the Grenadines]].Carolyn White.
